name: Mayors and Lord Mayors of the City of London
title: Mayors and Lord Mayors of the City of London
description: Every Mayor and Lord Mayor of the City of London since 1189, with year of election, mother livery company and notes.

rows.name: Henry FitzAilwin
rows.notes: First Mayor of London. Died in his twenty-fourth term.

rows.name: Jacob Alderman
rows.notes: Served until Trinity Sunday, when he died in office. His successor served as Mayor for the rest of the year.

rows.name: Salomon de Basing
rows.notes: Succeeded Jacob Alderman on or shortly after Trinity Sunday, and continued in office till the end of the year.

rows.name: Serlo le Mercer
rows.notes: Second to fifth terms of five.

rows.name: Richard Renger
rows.notes: Sixth and final term; died in office

rows.name: Gerard Bat
rows.notes: First term began 13 Jan 1239. Re-elected but not admitted to office in 1240

rows.name: Ralph Ashley
rows.notes: Three terms. Was a Grocer when Sheriff. Also "Eswy"

rows.name: Michael Tovey
rows.notes: First and second terms of four.

rows.name: Michael Tovey
rows.notes: Third and fourth terms of four.

rows.name: William FitzRichard
rows.notes: First of four terms as Royal Nominee.

rows.name: William FitzRichard
rows.notes: Second and third terms of four as Royal Nominee.

rows.name: Hugh FitzOtho
rows.notes: First of two terms as Royal Warden.

rows.name: William FitzRichard
rows.notes: Fourth and final term as Royal Nominee.

rows.name: Hugh FitzOtho
rows.notes: Second of two terms as Royal Warden.

rows.name: Henry le Walleis
rows.notes: Second to fourth of five terms.

rows.name: Sir Ralph Sandwich
rows.notes: First five terms of nine as Royal Warden.

rows.name: John le Breton
rows.notes: First of seven terms as Royal Warden.

rows.name: Sir Ralph Sandwich
rows.notes: Sixth to ninth terms as Royal Warden.

rows.name: John le Breton
rows.notes: Second to seventh terms of seven as Royal Warden.

rows.name: Sir John de Gisors
rows.notes: First and second terms of three.

rows.name: Sir Hamo de Chigwell
rows.notes: Second and third of seven terms.

rows.name: Sir Hamo de Chigwell
rows.notes: Fourth to sixth terms of seven.

rows.name: Sir John de Pulteney
rows.notes: First and second of four terms.

rows.name: Sir Andrew d'Aubrey
rows.notes: First and second of three terms.

rows.name: Simon Francis
rows.notes: First of two terms; the latter was in 1355 as Lord Mayor.

rows.name: Sir Thomas Legge
rows.notes: First of two terms; the latter was in 1354 as the first Lord Mayor.

rows.name: Sir John Lovekyn
rows.notes: First of three terms; the latter two were Lord Mayorships.

rows.name: Sir Thomas Legge
rows.notes: First Lord Mayor of London. Second of two terms, having initially served as Mayor of London.

rows.name: Simon Fraunceys
rows.notes: Second of two terms, having initially served as Mayor of London.

rows.name: Sir John Lovekyn
rows.notes: Second of three terms, having initially served as Mayor of London.

rows.name: Sir Adam de Bury
rows.notes: First two terms of three; impeached.

rows.name: Sir Nicholas Brembre
rows.notes: Second to fourth terms of four.

rows.name: Sir John Hende
rows.notes: First of two terms; deposed and imprisoned.

rows.name: Adam Bamme
rows.notes: Second of two term; died in office.

rows.name: Sir Richard Whittington
rows.notes: First of four terms; appointed by Richard II.

rows.name: Sir John Tate
rows.notes: Uncle of Sir Robert Tate (1488) and Sir John Tate (1496, 1514).

rows.name: Sir Robert Tate
rows.notes: Brother of Sir John Tate (1496, 1514); nephew of Sir John Tate (1473).

rows.name: Sir John Tate
rows.notes: First of two terms. Brother of Sir Robert Tate (1488); nephew of Sir John Tate (1473).

rows.name: Sir William Browne
rows.notes: Uncle of Sir William Browne (1514); died in office.

rows.name: Sir William Browne
rows.notes: Nephew of Sir William Browne (1507); died in office.

rows.name: Sir John Brydges
rows.notes: Born Brugge; also "Bridges. Father in law of Richard Sackville.

rows.name: Sir John Lyon or Lyons
rows.notes: First cousin of John Lyon (d. 1592) who was the founder of Harrow School

rows.name: Sir William Allen
rows.notes: Grandfather of Mary Box school founder

rows.name: Sir Richard Martin
rows.notes: First term, completing the term of Sir Martin Calthorpe.

rows.name: Sir Richard Martin
rows.notes: Second of two terms, completing that of Sir Cuthbert Buckle.

rows.name: Sir John Shorter
rows.notes: Died in office after a fall from his horse.

rows.name: Humphrey Parsons
rows.notes: First of two terms. Was the son of Sir John Parsons (1703).

rows.name: Humphrey Parsons
rows.notes: Second of two terms; died in office.

rows.name: William Ferneley Allen
rows.notes: In 1867, Michaelmas Day fell on the Sabbath. Alderman Allen elected on 28 September.

rows.name: George Nottage
rows.notes: Died in office; the last Lord Mayor to have done so.

rows.name: Sir Robert Fowler
rows.notes: Second of two terms; the last Lord Mayor to have served more than once.

rows.name: Sir Frank Bowater, 1st Baronet
rows.notes: Younger brother of Sir Vansittart Bowater (1913)

rows.name: Sir Rupert de la Bère, 1st Baronet
Sir Noël Bowater, 2nd Baronet
rows.notes: Nephew of Sir Vansittart Bowater (1913), son of Sir Frank Bowater (1938)

rows.name: Sir James Miller
rows.notes: Also served as Lord Provost of Edinburgh (1951–1954)

rows.name: Sir Ian Frank Bowater
rows.notes: Nephew of Sir Vansittart Bowater (1913), son of Sir Frank Bowater (1938), younger brother of Sir Noël Bowater (1953)

rows.name: Dame Mary Donaldson
rows.notes: First female Lord Mayor. Later Baroness Donaldson of Lymington

rows.name: The Lord Mountevans
rows.notes: Also a Goldsmith and elected Hereditary Member of the House of Lords.

rows.name: Sir William Russell
rows.notes: Served a two-year term due to the COVID-19 pandemic
